text:
Ashwin: Heads up — we are seeing a weird traffic pattern hitting the gpu-pool svc in us-west-2. Lots of retries from frontends -> svc -> endpoints, but only 3/12 GPUs taking ~95% of connections. latency spikes ~200-400ms east-west. Anyone else?
Maria: seen it on the dashboard, endpoints in nodepool-b keep getting hammered while others idle. 502s ramping.
Ben: can you paste the ipvs table from one of the affected nodes? suspect kube-proxy IPVS rules are rehashing oddly.
Ashwin: grabbing now, small excerpt: ```
IP Virtual Server version 1.2.1 (size=4096)
Prot LocalAddress:Port Scheduler Flags
  -> RemoteAddress:Port           Forward Weight ActiveConn InActConn
TCP  10.0.45.12:443 rr
  -> 10.2.7.3:8443              Route   1      132       5
  -> 10.2.8.6:8443              Route   1      3         0
  -> 10.2.9.4:8443              Route   1      2         0
TCP  10.0.45.12:10250 rr
  -> 10.2.7.3:10250             Route   1      120       4
  -> 10.2.8.6:10250             Route   1      4         0
```
Ashwin: notice the ActiveConn skew, despite endpoints having similar readiness.
Jun: also capture of conntrack on the frontend shows many entries pinned to 10.2.7.3. Could be asymmetric ECMP + ipvs-route interaction causing session pinning?
Maria: topology note: some nodes use RDMA NICs with jumbo MTU 9000; others are standard 1500. We rolled a kernel micropatch last week on nodepool-b (RDMA nodes).
Ben: that MTU mix + hairpin NAT can break path MTU/fragmentation and trigger retransmits that look like retries. Can we tcpdump on the svc VIP and endpoint 10.2.7.3? capture small window.
Ashwin: tcpdump snippet: ```
12:03:02.123 IP frontend1 > 10.2.7.3: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1452,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0], length 0
12:03:02.125 IP frontend1 > 10.2.7.3: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 8972,sackOK,TS val 123 ecr 0], length 0
12:03:02.130 IP 10.2.7.3 > frontend1: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```
Jun: see the MSS mismatch. Some SYNs advertise jumbo MSS because they choose RDMA path; something is rewriting enroute. That RST is from the endpoint rejecting weird seg sizes.
Ben: next steps: 1) disable hairpin mode on that kube-proxy instance and test (risk: might break node-local routing), 2) force homogeneous MTU on the RDMA pool (temporarily set 1500), 3) rotate kube-proxy to iptables mode for canary node and observe.
Maria: I'll start a canary: toggle mtu to 1500 on nodepool-b one node at a time, and drain gracefully. Keeping SRE oncall looped.
sre-bot: Incident pinned: INC-2026-1142 — svc daisychain/retry spike. Paging oncall.
Ashwin: also seeing a small number of services with NAT loopbacks causing daisy-chained forwarding: vip -> endpoint on same node -> hairpin back to vip -> different endpoint. That could amplify connection counts.
Jun: if hairpin+ipvs-route combine, a packet may be forwarded locally, then routed via kernel again, creating duplicate conn entries. Check /proc/sys/net/ipv4/conf/*/accept_local and rp_filter.
Ben: quick check commands: ```
sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_local
cat /proc/net/ip_vs
ipvsadm -Ln --stats
```
Maria: rolling mtus now on one node, will report in 10m. If that fixes it we should schedule a full rollback of the RDMA MTU change and add an explicit test in our canary suite.
Ashwin: also let's add a short e2e test: create ephemeral service with 1000 parallel conns from frontend to ensure even endpoint distribution. If it regresses, fail rollout.
Jun: agreed. Also file a kube-proxy bug if we can reproduce with a packet trace showing the daisychain. I can help craft the minimal repro.
Maria: update: after lowering MTU on one RDMA node, ActiveConn distribution normalized within ~2 minutes, 502s dropped. Rolling more nodes.
Ashwin: great, keep rolling. Postmortem TODOs: add MTU compatibility policy for mixed NIC types, add e2e distribution test, and consider automatic hairpin detection alert. :thumbsup:
